newsitem.title: UK: UK's CWS drops legal action against Hambros.
newsitem.headline: UK's CWS drops legal action against Hambros.

text.p: The Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) on Monday dropped legal proceedings against investment bank Hambros after the bank's chairman Sir Chips Keswick offered an unreserved apology over its conduct when it advised entrepreneur Andrew Regan's Galileo in its attempt to takeover CWS.

"The purpose of this letter is to offer my personal and the bank's unreserved apology and to assure you that we are taking the appropriate action to ensure that this will not happen again," Sir Chips writes.

Galileo's bid collapsed last week after CWS took legal action to block the use of information leaked to Regan by CWS executives and the withdrawal of key financial backing. On Friday, a High Court judge said the case represented a "gross, wilful and disgraceful breach of confidence".

CWS had originally said it would sue Hambros because the bank had "acted in breach of an equitable obligation of confidentiality to CWS. CWS said Hambros could have no credible grounds for believing that Regan had obtained documents about CWS legitimately.

Melmoth had attacked Hambros consistently during the saga, writing to the bank to demand explanations of its conduct on several occasions. On April 21, Keswick wrote to CWS, "I confirm that we continue to act as Lanica and Galileo's advisers. We appear to have differing views and I do not believe that any further correspondence on the questions you have raised is required."

But in Monday's letter, Keswick says, "Regretfully I have to say that it is quite clear to me the judgement exercised in Hambros, proceeding in the way that it did, fell well below our standards and those which you were entitled to expect from us."
